title: Building Better Bases: Change of Basis, Gram-Schmidt, and QR: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Building Better Bases: Change of Basis, Gram-Schmidt, and QR: Visual Guide

1. One Arrow Two Grids | one fixed arrow dragged over three grids in turn - standard, basis B and basis C - with its coordinates, the recipe those coordinates stand for, and the two basis vectors all read out live | a change of basis relabels coordinates and moves nothing, so the arrow, its length and the dimension of the space are untouched while the numbers describing it change, and getting those numbers is one matrix solve

2. Build The P Matrix | three pairs of bases showing B, C, C inverse, P = C inverse times B and its inverse as grids, with a vector’s B-coordinates slid and traced through standard coordinates into C and back | column j of P is b_j written in C, and C inverse times B is the order that lifts to standard then lowers into C, so writing it the other way round builds the opposite converter

3. Subtract The Shadow | v2 dragged anywhere around a chosen u1, drawing the shadow along u1 and the perpendicular leftover, with v2 dot u1, u1 dot u1, the scalar, and a live orthogonality check | the step removes only the component along u1 - it never rescales to length 1 and never flips a direction - so the leftover is orthogonal by construction, spans are preserved, and a zero result is linear dependence being reported rather than an arithmetic slip

4. Divide By The Norm | a vector slid in three dimensions against the three things people divide by (itself, the norm, the norm squared) with each resulting length bar-charted, plus an orthogonal set of norms 2, 5 and 10 under three rescaling rules | only dividing each vector by its own norm makes every length exactly 1; dividing by the norm squared or by one shared divisor leaves vectors that look plausible because the direction is right and only the length test separates them

5. Where R Comes From | four column pairs run through Gram-Schmidt with r11, q1, r12, v2, r22 and q2 shown step by step, the Q, R and Q-transpose-Q grids beside them, and a slider that stretches the second column | R is upper triangular because a_k is built from only q_1 through q_k, Q-transpose Q = I gives R = Q-transpose A with no inversion, and stretching a column leaves Q fixed while scaling that column of R - magnitude lands in R, direction lands in Q
